title: 1bfh19c
Maytham al-Tammar
hook: Imam Ali showed his date-selling friend the tree on which he would be hanged beforehand. In 60 AH that tree became the gallows.
scenes.0.text: Meysem Et-Tammar was a man who sold palm trees in the Kufa market. Tamar means palm tree. He was once a slave, but then he was freed. He owned his own bar, and he made a living off his own sweat. He was known for his closeness to **Ali**. Meissem would tell his customers what he had learned from him while selling dates. This little counter in the middle of the marketplace had become a lecture hall where the words of the Ehl-i Beyt were heard. Years later, that loyalty would cost him his life.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: acwx6t
Maytham
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.text: One day, **Ali** informed **Meysem** that he would be killed for his loyalty to the Ahl-i Beyt. He pointed to the palm tree he was going to hang from and told him his tongue would be cut off. My grandfather wasn't afraid of the news. Instead of running away, he often went to that tree after that day. He prayed at the base of the tree and watered the root. In Kufa, a common palm tree that everyone passed by became a place for Meysem to remember his death and his loyalty to his imam. This man, foreknowing his death, was looking at that tree with love.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: acwx6t
Maytham
scenes.2.text: After **Ali**'s martyrdom, hard times began in Kufa. By order of Mu'awiya, the governors were cursing Ali in the pulpits. **Hucr b. Adi** and his companions were killed for not accepting this curse. Defending Ali publicly in Kufa could have cost him his life. Many people were silent in fear. But **Meysem** kept talking about the virtues of the Ahl-i Beyt at the marketplace. He continued to narrate the words of Ali while selling his palm trees. While the miners were cursing, a small bench in the middle of the square continued to remember the name of Ali with affection.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: acwx6t
Maytham
scenes.3.text: In the 60th year of the Hijrah, Ubaydullah b. Ziyad, whom Yazid appointed as governor of Kufa, captured **Meysem**. He asked Meysem, who had been brought before him, to tell him that he had distanced himself from **Ali** and to tell him to leave. Tauberi is to announce that you're staying away from someone. That word could have saved Meysem's life. But that's not what Mayhem said. He did not deny Ali's name and openly expressed his love for him. His loyalty, which he had expressed for years in the marketplace, has not wavered in the face of death threats before the governor.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: acwx6t
Maytham
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 165bwyt
Ibn Ziyad
scenes.4.text: He hung himself from that palm tree that **Ali** showed him years ago. He didn't even shut up on the gallows. He called out to the crowd who had come to see him and continued to speak of the virtues of the Ahl-i Beyt. The crowd was gathering around him to listen to him. When Ibn Ziyad heard that **Meysem** was still speaking from the place where he was hanged, he became angry and ordered his tongue to be cut off. That's where Messem was martyred. The tree he watered for years was witness to his last words. Everything that Muhammad Ali predicted years ago came true.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: acwx6t
Maytham
scenes.5.text: Kufa, where Meysem was martyred, was soon to be the city that wrote letters to Husayn and invited him. Governor **Ibn Ziyad** forcibly dispersed the support behind the invitation. The pressure on a palm seller in the bazaar turned into a panic that engulfed the entire city when Muslim b. Aqil arrived in Kufa. Then an army from this city would surround Husayn at Karbala. Maysem went down in history as one of the first victims of that persecution.
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
shia.0.says: The news that Muhammad Ali will be hanged, his tongue cut off and the palm tree. That the Messiah prayed by that tree and watered it. He was hanged by Ibn Ziyad in 60 AH.
shia.1.says: That Meysem sold palm trees in Kufa, that he was a friend of Ali, that he refused the experience and was hanged.
shia.2.says: The prophecy, the tree, the hanging, the jewel, and the cutting of the tongue are translated in this compilation.
questions.0: Ali pointed to the palm tree that he was going to hang. Why do you think Mason went to that tree and watered its roots instead of running away?
questions.1: Hucr b. Adi and his friends were killed for refusing to accept the curse. Why do you think Meysem didn't stop talking at his desk when the price of defending Ali might have been death?
questions.2: When Ibn Ziyad heard that Meysem was still speaking from the place where he was hanged, he ordered his tongue to be cut off. Why do you think Ibn Ziyad was so angry at Meissem's speech?
summary: Maytham al-Tammar was a date seller in Kufa and a friend of Imam Ali. Imam Ali foretold to him that he would be hanged, that his tongue would be cut off, and the tree. In 60 AH Ibn Ziyad demanded tabarri. Maytham refused. He was martyred on the foretold tree.
key: Maytham al-Tammar: martyrdom on the foretold date palm
notes.0: Maytham al-Tammar was a freedman who sold dates in Kufa and was a friend of Imam Ali.
notes.1: Imam Ali foretold to him that he would be hanged, that his tongue would be cut off, and the date palm.
notes.2: In Mu'awiya's time Imam Ali was cursed from the pulpits. Hujr b. Adi was killed. Maytham did not keep silent.
notes.3: In 60 AH Ubaydullah b. Ziyad demanded tabarri. Maytham refused.
notes.4: The Messiah was hanged from the tree that was announced. They cut out his tongue. It's exactly what Ali reported.
sunni.0.says: The story of Meysem being bought and freed by Ali while he was a slave of a woman from Beni Esed; the story of Meysem being shown the palm tree and being told that Ali would hang him; the story of Meysem praying at the tree; the story of Ibn Ziyad being arrested and sentenced by Amr b. It is said that Hureys hanged him at the door, and his mouth was tied because he spoke of the virtues of the Hashemites while he was hanging.
sunni.0.grade: Ibn Hajar quotes this story from the Shia author al-Mu'awiya b. en-Nu'man's Menaqib and does not judge himself. So the news is coming from a Sunni source, but the Sunni mainstream doesn't consider it its own narrative.
